title: GitLab
subtitle: Self-hosted GitLab is where my agents open merge requests they are not allowed to merge, and where discovered defects are filed as issues.

stats.label: end-to-end runs from a worker's edit to an opened merge request
agent commits or merge requests against the main repository

lede: Agent Swarm needed to show that a coding agent on a local model could do real repository work without ever being able to merge it. I decided the merge request would be the boundary and GitLab, self-hosted, would be where a person sees the result. A worker agent edits, tests, commits and pushes to its own branch from a throwaway container. A separate, long-lived gatekeeper agent is the only holder of the repository credential, so a compromised or confused worker has nothing to leak; it checks the worker's request and opens the merge request through the GitLab API. The story A coding agent that never holds the keys tells it in full.
quote: I made the merge request the line agents cannot cross: they propose, a person merges.
evidence: Credential isolation for coding agents: a worker that edits, tests and pushes its own branch and a gatekeeper that alone holds the repository credential; 2 runs to merge request, 0 agent commits to main.
MCP tool design: one action-dispatched GitLab tool for issues, comments, labels, local git and merge requests, with a state that hands a problem back to a person.
author: Corey James
